report:
The original unrestricted optimal-damping task is not completed. The independently checked argument establishes A–E on the full declared rotational class R, together with obstructions for the unrestricted class. It supplies no sharp sufficient condition for arbitrary potentials. This is substantial partial progress, not a complete resolution under the supplied completion criterion. No substantive mathematical defect was found in the restricted proof.

The normalization and smooth formulas check out. Both the Xia–Zhang background and operator are divided by 2π, leaving scalar potentials unchanged. Direct differentiation gives the stated matrix, including the semipositive case without dividing by the vertical coefficient. The normalized radial density and fiber area give MAω(V)=12AΔ dx dΩ dA. The endpoint assumptions of the source's extension lemma are used for the constructed family; the local matrix calculation applies to arbitrary smooth invariant potentials at finite x. [Xia–Zhang](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.21053v1).

The new upper estimate is valid. Periodic integration gives ∫EΔ=m″+μ(1−μ)−e″/2. Fiber means and vertical Dirichlet integrals are smooth functions on the base, so m′ and e′ tend to zero at both radial ends. Consequently the nonnegative flux integrates to exactly one. Semipositivity gives Vxx≥−1; applying the resulting semiconvex inequality with displacement Vx and using V≤0 proves |Vx|²≤−2V. These facts give precisely 12Q(W) and 12QT(W), without assuming bounded unweighted mass or pointwise fiber constancy at the positive end.

The faster heat scale is admissible. The square estimate's hypotheses hold on each indicated transport region, including its application with κχ²; χ=0 is handled separately. At the new scale, the integrated defect is O(ℓ)+o(1), rather than o(1), and choosing the fixed c sufficiently small supplies all correction margins. The terminal cutoff error remains smaller than the background radial positivity because ℓ<1/(10e). The correction controls both the radial Schur complement and the tangential coefficient. Smooth extension and normalization follow from the actual endpoint behavior and the fiber mean. On the core, the completed square tends uniformly to one, the other negative terms are controlled, and the exact annular area is 3t/2. Thus the actual smooth measure has mass at least Dη⁻¹ at depths between Aη⁻² and Bη⁻². Matching T=Bη⁻² proves the necessary conditions for general decreasing weights, without regular-variation assumptions.

The single infinite-measure construction also checks out. Its correction has uniform local derivative control and the required global slope bound. The constant C* can be fixed before choosing scales. All recursive constraints can then be met at arbitrarily large values of √T W(T). Submean propagation through a finite connected chart cover gives the uniform L¹ bound without BMP. The decreasing series therefore has a genuine canonical quasi-psh limit, retaining the current margin 3ω/4. On every chosen core neighborhood, earlier terms are constant and the future series converges smoothly. The determinant inequality gives the actual local measure bound a_j³MAω(u_j). Normalization decreases depths and hence preserves the weighted lower bounds. Disjoint cores contribute at least one each, proving infinite weighted mass for one admissible potential.

The capacity argument uses the original capacity throughout. Both local comparisons are valid; the gluing parameters can be chosen sufficiently small to obtain a global test in [−1,0]. Compact central group convolution is smooth by transitivity, preserves the current inequality and rotational invariance, and its capacity convergence follows from the stated Markov argument. For bounded products, the telescoping integrals are controlled by mixed positive measures dominated by local capacity. Every lower degree therefore converges. Expanding against the smooth coefficient γ handles the nonclosed background; γ need not be closed. Quasi-continuity and uniform capacity domination justify the continuous depth weights. The foundational hypotheses match [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf); their operator differs by the positive factor 4π, which only rescales capacities and constants. The canonical limiting assertions agree with [Demailly](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf).

Canonical truncations and the task-granted compatible measures extend both upper estimates to every unbounded member of R. The capacity bound follows by splitting at depth T. For continuity, the truncation error is at most 24Q_{K−1}(W), including possible bounded-truncation mass on {u=−K}; no boundary-level mass is discarded.

The critical counterexample is an actual capacity-convergent sequence. The controlled correction masses tend to m=Kℓ>0. Near H, the limiting function has the local form m log|n|²−m log(1+|ζ|²)+constant, with n normal to H. This proves its genuine logarithmic extension and positive divisor current; the established margins control its smooth part, and its supremum is zero. Away from H, the heat exceptional sets shrink into tubes around the analytic section w=0, whose capacities tend to zero. Removing a small-capacity neighborhood of H proves uη→g in the original capacity. At the bounded critical regime, the full weighted measures are uniformly finite and have weak clusters. Their actual core masses force positive cluster mass on H, whereas νW,g(H)=0. When √t W(t) is unbounded, the single infinite measure obstructs a finite-measure map instead.

Accordingly, on R, individual finiteness and uniform total bounds hold exactly when √t W(t) is bounded; tails, uniform capacity absolute continuity and capacity-to-weak continuity hold exactly when √t W(t)→0. The stated power/logarithmic classifications follow. All necessary obstructions extend to the unrestricted class. Unrestricted sufficiency remains the task-granted integral condition, giving p>1 or p=1,a>1 in the power/logarithmic family; the intervening regimes remain unresolved here. The closed-elliptic diagnostic has consistent normalization and energy calculations, but establishes no additional global Hopf conclusion.

Harmless correction: the historical smooth-core note writes sup[−(Wη)x]₋ for the negative-slope bound. It must read sup[(Wη)x]₋. The current article already has the correct sign and proves that bound. Also, the tail passage at T=0 uses the total estimate directly, rather than an undefined Q_{−δ}. Neither correction changes the restricted argument.

passages.statement: On the scalar Hopf threefold, with dd^c_src=i∂bar∂ and ω_src=i∂bar∂s+i∂s∧bar∂s, s=log|z|², put ξ=z'/z0, w=log z0, x=log|ξ|² and μ=e^x/(1+e^x). For smooth real V(x,w), its local Hermitian matrix in the α_src-unit tangential, α_src-unit radial and ∂/∂w frame is [[(μ+Vx)/μ,0,0],[0,(μ+Vxx)/(μ(1−μ)),(μ+Vxbarw)/sqrt(μ(1−μ))],[0,(μ+Vwx)/sqrt(μ(1−μ)),1+Vwbarw]]. If V is independent of x for sufficiently negative x and constant in x,w for sufficiently positive x, it extends smoothly globally; positivity at ξ=0 is equivalent to 1+Vwbarw>0. Xia–Zhang, Lemma 2.2.

For E=C/(Z+2πiZ), probability Haar area dA=i dw∧dbarw/(4π), k_t(w)=(2/t)Σλ exp(−|w−λ|²/t), and Fη(t,w)=−η∫t∞(k_r(w)−1)dr, 0<η<1/10, one has Fη,t=Fη,wbarw=η(k_t−1), (log k_t)wbarw≥−1/t, and ||∂t^a Fη(t,·)||C^m≤C_a,m ηe^(−t/4) for t≥1 and fixed nonnegative integers a,m, uniformly in η. Xia–Zhang, Lemma 3.1.

For k_t(w)=(2/t)Σλ∈Z+2πiZ exp(−|w−λ|²/t), absolute constants C0≥1 and C exist such that tk_t≤C0 exp(−|t∂barw log k_t|²/(C0t)) for 0<t≤1. If 0<κ<1/(200C0), 0<η<1/10, 0<t≤1, 1/2≤μ≤1, σ=sqrt((2κ/η)log(1/(ηt))), h=ηk_t and ζ=(σ/μ)t∂barw log k_t, then κtk_t−μ²(1−η)h|ζ−(1−η)^−1|²/(1−η+h)≤Cκ exp(−1/(Cσ²t)), uniformly in all these parameters and w. Xia–Zhang, Lemmas 3.2–3.3.

For Ω⊂C^n and locally bounded genuine psh p1,…,pk, k≤n, their Bedford–Taylor mixed product is a positive closed current, local and symmetric multilinear in its arguments, and weakly continuous under simultaneous decreasing locally bounded psh limits. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2.

For locally bounded psh p,q on Ω⊂C^n and compactly supported smooth (n−k,n−k)-forms φ, 1≤k≤n, ∫φ[(dd^cp)^k−(dd^cq)^k]=Σl=0^(k−1)∫(p−q)dd^cφ∧(dd^cp)^l∧(dd^cq)^(k−1−l). Bedford–Taylor, Corollary 2.8 and its mixed-degree integration-by-parts consequence.
passages.quote: holds for smooth u and v

passages.statement: For K compactly contained in Ω⊂C^n, bounded psh p1,…,pk, k≤n, and the Euclidean Kähler form β, ∫K dd^cp1∧⋯∧dd^cpk∧β^(n−k)≤C_K,Ω,k∏i||pi||L∞(Ω). Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.10.

On a bounded domain Ω⊂C^n, every genuine psh function is quasi-continuous for relative Bedford–Taylor capacity: for each ε>0 there is an open O⊂Ω with C(O,Ω)<ε such that its restriction to Ω minus O is continuous. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 3.5.
On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain Ω⊂C^n, every locally pluripolar set has zero outer Bedford–Taylor capacity. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 6.9.
On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex Ω⊂C^n, if compact subsets Kj decrease to K, then C(Kj,Ω) decreases to C(K,Ω); also C*(K,Ω)=C(K,Ω). Bedford–Taylor, Proposition 6.4.

On an open Ω⊂C^n, a decreasing sequence of genuine psh functions has a genuine locally integrable psh pointwise limit whenever the limit is not identically −∞ on any component. A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. The cone Psh(Ω)∩L1_loc(Ω) is closed in L1_loc, and its L1_loc-bounded subsets are relatively compact. Demailly, I.4.17, I.5.4 and I.5.8–5.9.
